title: Database connection pool exhausted
description: Production PostgreSQL connection pool hit max limit. All API endpoints returning 500. Error: 'too many connections'.
root_cause: A deployment of payments-service v2.3.1 introduced a connection leak in the transaction rollback path. Connections were not being returned to the pool on rollback.
resolution:
1. Increased max_connections temporarily in postgres config
2. Rolled back payments-service to v2.3.0
3. Restarted connection pool manager
4. Added connection leak detection via pg_stat_activity monitoring
lessons_learned: Always verify connection cleanup in error paths before deploying. Added connection pool monitoring to deployment checklist.

title: Memory leak in order processing worker
description: order-worker pods hitting OOMKilled every 4-6 hours. Memory usage grows linearly from ~200MB to 2GB.
root_cause: Kafka consumer was accumulating message offsets in an in-memory dict that was never cleared. Introduced in v1.8.0 with the new at-least-once delivery feature.
resolution:
1. Added max offset cache size with LRU eviction
2. Deployed hotfix v1.8.1
3. Set Kubernetes memory limits to 1.5GB to catch future regressions faster
4. Added memory metrics dashboard
lessons_learned: Any unbounded in-memory accumulation must have a max-size and eviction policy. Added to code review checklist.

title: Redis cache stampede causing API latency spike
description: p99 latency jumped from 80ms to 4200ms. Redis hit rate dropped from 94% to 12%. Thousands of cache misses hitting the database simultaneously.
root_cause: A scheduled job deleted all product category cache keys at midnight for a cache refresh. All in-flight requests then hit the DB simultaneously.
resolution:
1. Re-populated Redis cache manually from a DB snapshot
2. Implemented probabilistic early expiration (jitter on TTL)
3. Replaced bulk cache deletion with rolling key expiration
lessons_learned: Never delete cache keys in bulk. Use jitter on TTL and rolling expiration. Cache warming should be gradual.

title: Kubernetes node not ready — disk pressure
description: 3 of 12 worker nodes went NotReady. Pods evicted. 30% capacity loss. Alert: 'node disk pressure'.
root_cause: Docker image layers from failed CI builds accumulated over 3 weeks without pruning. /var/lib/docker reached 95% capacity.
resolution:
1. Ran 'docker system prune -af' on affected nodes
2. Added daily cron for docker image pruning
3. Set Kubernetes eviction threshold to 85% disk
4. Added disk usage alert at 75%
lessons_learned: Container runtimes need periodic pruning. Automated cleanup should be standard for all nodes.

title: Certificate expiry causing auth failures
description: All OAuth token validations failing. Users being logged out across the platform. Error: 'certificate expired'.
root_cause: TLS certificate for auth.internal expired. Auto-renewal via cert-manager failed silently due to a misconfigured ClusterIssuer after a recent Kubernetes upgrade.
resolution:
1. Manually renewed certificate via Let's Encrypt
2. Restarted cert-manager and verified ClusterIssuer config
3. Tested renewal flow end-to-end
4. Added cert expiry monitoring with 30/7/1 day alerts
lessons_learned: cert-manager ClusterIssuer config must be verified after any K8s upgrade. Multi-layered cert expiry alerts are non-negotiable.

title: Slow query degrading checkout performance
description: Checkout page timing out for 15% of users. DB CPU at 95%. Slow query log showing full table scan on orders table.
root_cause: A migration added a new `status_updated_at` column but the query filtering on it was missing an index. At 50M rows, this caused full table scans.
resolution:
1. Added index CONCURRENTLY on (status_updated_at, user_id)
2. Verified query plan changed to index scan
3. DB CPU dropped to 18%
4. Added explain-plan checks to migration review process
lessons_learned: Every migration adding a new column that will be queried must include the appropriate index. Migration PRs now require query plan analysis.

title: Message queue backlog — notification service lag
description: Notification delivery delayed by 40+ minutes. SQS queue depth growing at 10,000 messages/min. Dead letter queue filling up.
root_cause: A third-party email provider (SendGrid) enforced new rate limits (200 req/s) without notice. notification-service was sending at 1,200 req/s. Failures went to retry queue, creating a feedback loop.
resolution:
1. Implemented token bucket rate limiter at 180 req/s
2. Cleared DLQ by replaying with throttling
3. Added circuit breaker for SendGrid calls
4. Subscribed to SendGrid status page and API changelog
lessons_learned: Always implement rate limiting on third-party API calls. Subscribe to status pages and changelogs for all external dependencies.

title: Deployment rollout caused config drift
description: After deploying inventory-service v3.1.0, 25% of pods using old config. Mixed behavior causing data inconsistency in stock levels.
root_cause: ConfigMap was not updated before the deployment rollout. Rolling update started with a mix of old and new pods reading different feature flag values.
resolution:
1. Paused rollout
2. Updated ConfigMap with correct values
3. Forced restart of all pods to ensure uniform config
4. Added config validation step to deployment pipeline
lessons_learned: ConfigMap updates must precede deployment rollouts. Added config health check as a pre-deployment gate.

title: DNS resolution failure in staging
description: Internal service discovery broken in staging cluster. All inter-service HTTP calls failing with 'no such host'.
root_cause: CoreDNS pods crashed after a node pool upgrade changed the CPU limits in the system namespace. CoreDNS was OOMKilled and not restarting due to crashloop backoff.
resolution:
1. Manually deleted crashlooping CoreDNS pods to force reschedule
2. Increased CoreDNS resource limits
3. Verified DNS resolution across all namespaces
4. Added CoreDNS health checks to cluster monitoring
lessons_learned: Node pool upgrades can reset system namespace resource limits. Always verify critical system pods after cluster maintenance.

title: API gateway 502 errors after traffic spike
description: Super Bowl ad drove 10x traffic spike. API gateway returning 502 for 40% of requests. Backend healthy but upstream timeout errors in logs.
root_cause: API gateway upstream timeout was set to 30s. Under high load, backend response times rose to 25-35s. Gateway was timing out valid but slow responses.
resolution:
1. Increased gateway upstream timeout to 60s
2. Enabled autoscaling on backend services (min 5, max 50 pods)
3. Added request queuing with backpressure
4. Implemented load shedding for non-critical endpoints
lessons_learned: Traffic spike scenarios must be load-tested. Autoscaling configuration and timeout values need to be reviewed before major campaigns.

title: S3 bucket policy change blocked media uploads
description: User profile photo uploads failing with 403. 'Access Denied' in S3 access logs. Affecting ~8,000 users/hour.
root_cause: A security audit applied a new restrictive S3 bucket policy that blocked the IAM role used by media-service. The change was not tested against application roles.
resolution:
1. Identified the blocking policy condition via CloudTrail
2. Added explicit Allow for media-service IAM role in bucket policy
3. Verified uploads successful
4. Added S3 permission smoke tests to deployment pipeline
lessons_learned: Security policy changes must be tested against all application IAM roles before applying to production. Added S3 permission regression tests.

title: Elasticsearch index corruption after shard failure
description: Product search returning stale/incorrect results. ES cluster health showing RED. Two primary shards unassigned.
root_cause: An underlying EBS volume hit an IOPS limit and produced write errors, corrupting two primary shards. Replica shards could not be promoted due to a cluster setting (cluster.routing.allocation.enable: none) left from a previous maintenance.
resolution:
1. Re-enabled shard allocation
2. Forced replica promotion on the two unassigned shards
3. Verified index integrity with _cat/shards API
4. Triggered full reindex from database source of truth
lessons_learned: cluster.routing.allocation must be re-enabled as the FIRST step after any ES maintenance. Added post-maintenance checklist to runbook.
